YouGov (pollster's own published results — primary source) — published 29 September 2026, confirmed from the in-page byline "Matthew Smith - 29 September 2026" and the fieldwork note. Daily-question tables timestamped 2026-09-29T19:15:00Z. Search highlights.
"Britons support changing triple lock to fund care service by 48% to 28%"
Fieldwork: 29 September 2026. Sample: online survey of 4,503 adults aged 18+ in Great Britain. Commissioned by YouGov.
- National Care Service free at the point of use: 74% support, 11% opposed.
- Changing the triple lock to a double lock (inflation or 2.5%), asked in isolation: 43% in favour, 30% opposed. A YouGov survey in May asking the same question found a much lower lead of 35% vs 30%.
- The same change explicitly linked to funding a National Care Service: 48% support, 28% opposed.
- By 2024 vote: backed by 66% of Labour voters, 67% of Lib Dems, 58% of Greens, 37% of Conservatives, 27% of Reform UK voters.
Question wordings as published: "The triple lock on pensions means the government guarantees that pensions payments will rise by whatever is highest - earnings, inflation, or 2.5%. Would you support or oppose changing this, so pensions only increase by whatever is highest out of inflation or 2.5%?" and "Andy Burnham has announced he plans to change the triple lock in 2030 so that pensions only increase by whatever is highest out of inflation or 2.5%. The money will be used to help fund part of a national care service. Do you support or oppose this policy?"
